newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS ACTIVATE RELIEVER JOSE MESA.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS ACTIVATE RELIEVER JOSE MESA.

text.p: The Cleveland Indians activated Jose Mesa before Friday's home opener against the Anaheim Angles, two days after their ace relief pitcher was acquitted of charges of rape, gross sexual imposition and theft.

Mesa had been scheduled to go to trial again Monday on a separate charge of carrying a concealed weapon, but the Ohio judge presiding over the case ruled police improperly seized the gun in a search of the pitcher's vehicle when he was arrested last December.

Mesa had not been with the team since his rape trial began March 31, two days before the Indians' regular season began in Oakland. He had been working out at Jacobs Field evenings to stay in shape but will not likely see action Friday.
Mesa and a friend were indicted on charges stemming from a December 22 incident in a Lakewood, Ohio motel. But the Dominican Republic native was acquitted of all charges Wednesday.

He appeared in 69 games for the Indians last season, recording 39 saves and posting a 2-7 record with a 3.73 ERA. Mesa finished second in voting for the 1995 American League Cy Young Award when he posted a club-record 46 saves in helping the club reach the World Series.
